w: Renamed Rabindra Setu for the poet Tagore in 1965, nobody in Kolkata actually calls it that -- it's still just the Howrah Bridge, and everybody uses it: roughly 100,000 vehicles and 150,000 pedestrians cross daily, making this 1943 steel cantilever the busiest of its kind on Earth.
s: Officially Rabindra Setu. Nobody calls it that.
_facts: Commissioned 1943, replaced a pontoon bridge
Renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965 after Rabindranath Tagore, still popularly called Howrah Bridge
Carries about 100,000 vehicles and 150,000+ pedestrians daily
Busiest cantilever bridge in the world

w: The story goes that when Shiva danced in grief carrying Sati's corpse, Vishnu's discus sliced her body apart -- and a toe from her right foot fell here, consecrating one of Bengal's four Adi Shaktipeeths. Hundreds of thousands still crowd in for Kali Puja and Durga Puja every year.
s: Where a goddess's toe is said to have fallen.
_facts: One of 51 Shakti Pithas, one of four Adi Shaktipeeths
Legend: toe of Sati's right foot fell here after Vishnu's chakra split her body
Draws hundreds of thousands during Kali Puja, Durga Puja and other occasions

n: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden
w: Renamed for the physicist-botanist Jagadish Chandra Bose, this Shibpur garden has been cataloguing the subcontinent's flora since the British called it the Royal Botanic Garden, Calcutta -- more than 12,000 specimens now spread across 109 hectares, tended by the Botanical Survey of India.
_facts: Previously Indian Botanic Garden, Calcutta Botanic Garden, Royal Botanic Garden Calcutta
Over 12,000 specimens across 109 hectares
Managed by the Botanical Survey of India
_sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden

w: India's oldest formal zoo has been open since 1876, but its most famous resident predated the place itself: Adwaita, an Aldabra giant tortoise reputed to be over 250 years old when he died here in 2006 -- briefly making this modest 46-acre park home to one of the planet's oldest living animals.
s: Home to a tortoise reputed to be 250-plus.
_facts: India's oldest formally stated zoological park, open since 1876
Covers 18.811 ha (46.48 acres)
Home to Adwaita, an Aldabra giant tortoise reputed to be over 250 years old at death in 2006
Runs a captive breeding project for the Manipur brow-antlered deer

w: Wall-to-wall marble under a name that undersells it: this nineteenth-century North Kolkata mansion is lined floor to ceiling with imported stone and sculpture, one of the best-preserved grand houses left from the city's colonial heyday -- still standing on Muktaram Babu Street exactly as built.
s: A 19th-century mansion floored entirely in marble.
_facts: Palatial 19th-century mansion at 46 Muktaram Babu Street
One of the best-preserved, most elegant houses of 19th-century Calcutta
Famous for marble walls, floors, and sculptures

w: Everyone still half-remembers this South Kolkata lake and park by its old name, Dhakuria -- before the city renamed it for Bengal's Nobel-winning poet. Rabindra Sarobar now anchors the neighborhood, hemmed in by Southern Avenue, the railway line, and Dhakuria itself, exactly as it always was.
s: Dhakuria Lake, renamed for the poet Tagore.
_facts: Formerly known as Dhakuria Lake
Artificial lake, garden and park in South Kolkata
Named after Nobel laureate poet Rabindranath Tagore
Flanked by Southern Avenue, Shyamaprasad Mukherjee Road, Dhakuria, and the Kolkata Suburban Railway tracks

w: Once known simply as the Dharmatala Mosque, this Kolkata landmark was renamed for Tipu Sultan, the famed ruler of Mysore, on the street that still carries the old name. It's known today for the architectural and cultural heritage relics preserved inside its walls.
s: Named for a Mysore ruler, on Dharmatala Street.
_facts: Officially Tipu Sultan Shahi Mosque, formerly known as the Dharmatala Mosque
Located at 185 Dharmatala Street
Named after Tipu Sultan, ruler of Mysore
Renowned for architectural and cultural heritage relics

w: Completed in 1926 at the junction of Zakaria Street and Rabindra Sarani, the Nakhoda Masjid is Kolkata's principal mosque -- a Hanafi Sunni landmark rising out of the crowded wholesale lanes of Burrabazar, where the trade never really lets up, even at the mosque's own doorstep.
s: Kolkata's principal mosque, in the thick of Burrabazar.
_facts: Sunni mosque in Chitpur area of Burrabazar
Completed 1926
Principal mosque of Kolkata, affiliated with the Hanafi school
At the intersection of Zakaria Street and Rabindra Sarani

w: Opened in 1840 when Calcutta was the seat of the East India Company, the self-styled 'Jewel of the East' hosted the era's notable travelers through the Raj and beyond. The state took over its management after independence; a private buyer later restored it, reopening in 2013 as the LaLiT Great Eastern.
_facts: Colonial-era hotel established 1840/41
Called 'Jewel of the East' in its heyday
State government took over management after 1947 independence
Sold to a private company in 2005, reopened 2013 after renovation

w: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated this circular Chowringhee Road hall in 1963, its shape modeled loosely on the Buddhist stupa at Sanchi. Kolkata just calls it 'taramandal' -- the star house -- still Asia's largest planetarium, running sky shows in English, Bengali and Hindi beside the Victoria Memorial.
s: Asia's largest planetarium, shaped like a stupa.
_facts: Circular structure loosely styled on the Buddhist stupa at Sanchi
Adjacent to Victoria Memorial, St Paul's Cathedral and the Maidan
Largest planetarium in Asia, second largest in the world
Inaugurated 2 July 1963 by PM Jawaharlal Nehru
Popularly known as taramandal; shows in English, Bengali and Hindi

w: One of Kolkata's biggest Durga Pujas fills this South Kolkata playground each autumn, even as the park itself keeps shrinking to a club, a public toilet, a restaurant. Small consolation: in 2015 it became the city's first spot lit by grid-connected, battery-less solar streetlights.
s: A shrinking park with Kolkata's biggest Durga Puja.
_facts: Playground between Rashbehari Avenue and Sarat Bose Road
Hosts one of the biggest Durga Puja celebrations in the city
Encroached over the years by a club, public toilet and restaurant
In Feb 2015 got Kolkata's first grid-connected, battery-less solar streetlights

w: Still known to old-timers simply as the Grand, this Chowringhee Road landmark has worn its British-era elegance since long before the Oberoi Group's name went up over the door -- one of the handful of buildings in the city everyone still points to as pure, unmistakable Calcutta grandeur.
_facts: Originally the Grand Hotel, now the Oberoi Grand, on Chowringhee Road
Elegant British-era building
Owned by EIH Ltd, the Oberoi chain

w: Kolkata's Chinatown grew up around an unlikely trade: tanneries, run for generations by families of Hakka Chinese origin who settled in this pocket of the city's east. The leatherworks have mostly faded, but the Hakka Chinese community that built the neighborhood remains its story.
s: Kolkata's Chinatown, built on the tannery trade.
_facts: Region in East Kolkata
Traditionally housed many tanneries
Tanneries owned by people of Hakka Chinese origin
